{{Use British English|date=June 2017}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=June 2017}}
'''Roger John Cashmore''' {{postnominals|country=GBR|size=100%|CMG|FRSA}} (born 22 August 1944) is the chair of the [[United Kingdom Atomic Energy Authority]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.uk-atomic-energy.org.uk/about_corp_gov.html | publisher = UK Atomic Energy Authority | title = Corporate Governance | accessdate = 7 October 2010 }}</ref> Previously he was [[Principal (college)|principal]] of [[Brasenose College, Oxford]], and professor of experimental [[physics]] at the [[University of Oxford]].
His interests include the origin of the masses of particles and the [[Higgs boson]].<ref>{{cite news | url = https://www.independent.co.uk/news/science/searching-for-the-god-particle-in-a-giant-underground-cavern-540192.html | date = 9 June 2003 | author = Steve Connor | newspaper = [[The Independent]] | title = Searching for the 'God particle' in a giant underground cavern }}</ref>

==Education==
{{unreferencedsect|date=September 2026}}
Cashmore was educated at [[Dudley Boys Grammar School]], [[St John's College, Cambridge]] ([[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] 1965, [[Master of Arts (Oxbridge)|MA]]), [[Balliol College, Oxford]], and [[University College, Oxford]] ([[Doctor of Philosophy|DPhil]] 1969, Weir Junior Research Fellow, [[1851 Research Fellowship|1851 Research Fellow]]). His doctoral thesis was entitled ''A study of inelastic pion-proton interactions in the range 600–800 MeV/c''.

==Academic career==

He was a research associate at [[Stanford Linear Accelerator Center]] 1969–74. Returning to [[University of Oxford|Oxford]] he was a research officer (1974–78), teaching lecturer at [[Christ Church, Oxford|Christ Church]] (1976–78), [[Fellow#Oxford, Cambridge and Dublin|senior research fellow]] at [[Merton College, Oxford|Merton]] (1977–79), and [[Fellow#Oxford, Cambridge and Dublin|fellow and tutor]] at [[Balliol College, Oxford|Balliol]] and university lecturer in physics (1979–90). He was appointed [[Reader (academic rank)|reader]] in experimental physics in 1990 and professor of experimental physics in 1991. He was also head of particle and nuclear physics 1991–96 and chair of the Department of Physics 1997–99. He was appointed principal of [[Brasenose College, Oxford|Brasenose]] from 2002 onwards. Cashmore also served as director of research and deputy director general at [[CERN|Organisation européenne pour la recherche nucléaire (CERN)]] from 1999 to 2004. During his term, several agreements took place with China's and Pakistan's to be of the most important.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Major agreement made with China|journal=CERN Courier|date=June 1999|volume=39|issue=5|page=6|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1732958?ln=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=News: CERN and Pakistan strengthen agreement|journal=CERN Courier|date=July 2000|volume=40|issue=6|page=9|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1733104?ln=en}}</ref> In 2002 he became co-chairman of the CERN-JINR joint scientific committee after Jim Allaby's retirement.<ref>{{cite journal|title=People: meetings|journal=CERN Courier|date=February 2002|volume=42|issue=1|page=31|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1733280}}</ref>

He was visiting professor at the [[Vrije Universiteit Brussel]] in 1982, [[Science and Engineering Research Council|Science and Engineering Research Council Senior Research Fellow]] 1982–87, a guest scientist at [[Fermilab|Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory]] 1986–87, and held an [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]] Research Award 1995/96. 

[[Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom|HM The Queen]] appointed Roger Cashmore [[Order of St Michael and St George|Companion of the Most Distinguished Order of St Michael and St George]] for services to international co-operation in particle physics in the New Year Honours List 2004. He was awarded the [[Institute_of_Physics#Awards|C.V. Boys Prize]] in 1983. He was elected a [[Institute of Physics|Fellow of the Institute of Physics]] in 1985, a member of Academia Europa in 1992, a [[Royal Society of Arts|Fellow of the Royal Society of Arts]] in 1996, and a [[Royal Society|Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 1998. He is a member of the advisory council for the [[Campaign for Science and Engineering]].<ref name="CaSE Advisory Council">{{cite web|url=http://www.sciencecampaign.org.uk/about/who/advisory.htm|title=Advisory Council of the Campaign for Science and Engineering|accessdate=11 February 2011|archive-date=28 August 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100828110110/http://www.sciencecampaign.org.uk/about/who/advisory.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Controversy==
Cashmore's final years at Oxford were marked by allegations of improper claims for travel expenses, following the publication in May 2010 of a leaked report from an investigation committee at Brasenose College.<ref name='CherwellExp'>{{cite news | first = Camilla | last = Turner | title = Brasenose head in expenses leak | date = 27 May 2010 | work = [[Cherwell (newspaper)|Cherwell]]| publisher = [[Oxford Student Publications Limited]] | url = http://www.cherwell.org/news/2010/05/27/brasenose-head-in-expenses-leak  | accessdate = 27 October 2011 | quote = Report claims unauthorised foreign trips for Professor Cashmore and his wife}}</ref><ref name='TelegraphExp'>{{cite news | first = Stephen | last = Adams |author2=Camilla Turner  | title = Oxford principal faced travel expenses investigation | date = 31 May 2010 | url = https://www.telegraph.co.uk/journalists/stephen-adams/7786330/Oxford-principal-faced-travel-expenses-investigation.html | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20100615235231/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/journalists/stephen-adams/7786330/Oxford-principal-faced-travel-expenses-investigation.html | url-status = dead | archive-date = 15 June 2010 | work = [[The Daily Telegraph]] | accessdate = 27 October 2011 | quote = An Oxford University college principal has been investigated over his travel expenses for a string of trips to Pakistan, north America and Greece.}}</ref> Cashmore denied any misuse of expenses, claiming that the report contained a number of inaccuracies.<ref name='TelegraphExp'/> During October 2010 Brasenose College announced that Cashmore would be taking research leave.<ref name='TelegraphLeave'>{{cite news | first = Graeme | last = Paton |author2=Camilla Turner  | title = Expenses row Oxford don takes study leave | date = 6 October 2010 | url = https://www.telegraph.co.uk/education/educationnews/8046359/Expenses-row-Oxford-don-takes-study-leave.html | work = [[The Daily Telegraph]] | accessdate = 27 October 2011 | quote = An Oxford University college principal has taken a year-long sabbatical after being investigated over his travel expenses.}}</ref> The college denied that there was any link between this decision and the previous allegations concerning expenses, but a second leaked document indicated that the governing body of the college had passed a motion of no confidence in Cashmore,<ref name='TelegraphLeave'/><ref name='CherwellCash'>{{cite news | first = Camilla | last = Turner | title = Even more cash for Cashmore | date = 15 October 2010 | work = [[Cherwell (newspaper)|Cherwell]]| publisher = [[Oxford Student Publications Limited]] | url = http://www.cherwell.org/news/2010/10/09/even-more-cash-for-cashmore  | accessdate = 27 October 2011 | quote = Brasenose Principal will be paid £1250 per day for a post advertised just two days after expenses scandal}}</ref> who subsequently applied for the post of chairman of the United Kingdom Atomic Energy Authority.<ref name='CherwellCash'/><ref name='CherwellWhat'>{{cite news | title = The week that was: Cash for Cashmore | date = 14 October 2010 | work = [[Cherwell (newspaper)|Cherwell]]| publisher = [[Oxford Student Publications Limited]] | url = http://www.cherwell.org/comment/2010/10/15/the-week-that-was-cash-for-cashmore  | accessdate = 27 October 2011}}</ref> A spokesperson for Brasenose College said "The members of the standing Sub-Committee were dismayed that their report to the Governing Body had been leaked to the press."<ref name='CherwellCash'/> The college also commented that "The [expenses] report did not conclude that the Principal had submitted any claims for travel expenses that were not genuine. The members of the Sub-Committee are confident that there is no question of impropriety on his part."<ref name='CherwellCash'/>

On 9 December 2010 Brasenose's acting principal, [[Alan Bowman (classicist)|Alan Bowman]], announced Cashmore's retirement from his role as principal at the end of the 2010–2011 academic year "to focus on his role as Chairman of the United Kingdom Atomic Energy Authority and to return to his research interests at [[CERN]] and the [[Large Hadron Collider|LHC]] (Large Hadron Collider), at what is a particularly exciting time for particle physics."<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.bnc.ox.ac.uk/288/about-brasenose-31/news-152/retirement-of-the-principal-professor-cashmore-872.html | title = Retirement of the Principal, Professor Cashmore | date = 9 December 2010 | publisher = [[Brasenose College, Oxford]] }}</ref> This announcement led to the republication of previous allegations.<ref
